# Feature: Executable Agent Provider Foundation

## 1. Feature Goal

**ID**: FEAT-022
**Source Plan**: `.spec-lite/plan_agentic.md`

Replace the non-executable agent scaffolding with a real, thin provider seam backed by the `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent` SDK. After this feature, Yantra can open a genuine Pi agent session against pinned, Yantra-owned Pi runtime paths, invoke a registered custom tool, receive normalized (sanitized) events, and fail with actionable typed errors instead of silently degrading to a null client. This is the delivery-order root: every later agentic feature builds on this seam.

> **Plan override note (plan §preamble)**: this feature operates under the plan's explicit override of `memory.md` — the SDK package is `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent` (not `pi-agent-core`), and `packages/agent` MAY import `packages/core`. The `core -> agent` direction remains forbidden.

## 2. Data Model (Granular)

No relational storage. The "data model" is the seam contract (plan §4, authoritative) plus the pinned Pi environment layout.

### Entities & Attributes

- **AgentProvider / AgentSession** (TypeScript interfaces, `packages/agent/src/provider/types.ts`):
  - `AgentSession.id` (string) — provider session identity.
  - `AgentSession.logPath` (string) — absolute path to the Pi session JSONL.
  - `run(prompt) -> AgentRunResult`, `subscribe(listener)`, `abort()`, `close()`.
- **AgentSessionOptions**: `runId`, `runDir`, `cwd`, `model: AgentModelSelection`, `auth: AgentAuthSelection`, `systemPrompt` — all `readonly`.
- **AgentModelSelection**: `provider` (string), `id` (string), `thinking?` (string).
- **AgentAuthSelection**: `{ mode: 'managed' }` | `{ mode: 'runtime-key'; secretRef: string }`.
- **AgentEvent** (closed discriminated union): `tool_started`, `tool_finished`, `assistant_text`, `turn_finished`, `failed` — exactly as defined in plan §4; every payload post-sanitizer.
- **AgentRunResult**: `outcome: 'completed' | 'failed' | 'aborted'`, `stopReason` (string), `usage: AgentUsage`.
- **AgentUsage**: `turns` (number), `inputTokens?`, `outputTokens?`, `costUsd?`.
- **AgentError**: `code` (string, one of plan §9 codes), `message` (string, sanitized).

### Pi environment layout (Yantra-owned, plan §4/§8.11)

```text
~/.local/share/yantra/pi/          # pinned agentDir (namespaced per platform data dir)
  auth.json                        # managed credentials (Yantra-owned by default)
  models.json                      # custom/local model definitions (Ollama etc.)
  sessions/                        # only used if run-local placement needs staging
```

- Settings are supplied **in-memory** with pinned overrides — no `settings.json` is read from disk, neither global `~/.pi/agent/` nor project `.pi/`.
- Opt-in config key (in `~/.config/yantra/config.yaml`) may point `managed` auth at an existing personal pi `auth.json`; never a default.

### Indexes & Constraints

- Discriminant exhaustiveness on `AgentEvent` and `AgentAuthSelection` enforced by compile-time `never` checks in tests.
- Seam must not expand beyond plan §4 without a demonstrated consumer (boundary review rule).

## 4. Dependencies

- None among the agentic features (this is the root).
- Existing infrastructure: `packages/core` sanitizer (event payload sanitization), secrets resolver (`runtime-key` mode), Yantra data-dir path helpers.
- **User checkpoint (memory rule)**: confirm the exact pinned SDK version with the user before installing.

## 6. Cross-Cutting Concerns

- **Auth**: model credentials only — via pinned `AuthStorage` (managed), `setRuntimeApiKey` (runtime-key from Yantra `SecretRef`), or env vars (recorded as `auth_source: environment` by FEAT-023). Website credentials are out of scope here.
- **Error Handling**: all adapter entry points return/throw the typed errors above; `Result<T, E>` at seam boundaries per memory; no silent degradation for agentic commands.
- **Logging**: pino `info` for session open/close, `debug` for event mapping; never log prompt text, keys, or raw Pi payloads. The run directory remains the observability artifact (FEAT-023 owns persistence).
- **Security**: plan §8.1/§8.2/§8.11 are acceptance-level here — built-ins disabled, zero ambient resources, pinned paths. The environment enumeration test is the enforcement.
